coverage_notes:
STRONGEST SOURCE. The decisive find is Oklahoma's own athletics-site staff page, headed "2000 Football Staff," recovered from the Wayback Machine at https://web.archive.org/web/20010212052906/http://soonersports.fansonly.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/okla-m-footbl-mttcoaches.html (archived Feb 12, 2001, five weeks after the Jan 3, 2001 Orange Bowl). An identical listing exists in a pre-season snapshot (Aug 23, 2000) at https://web.archive.org/web/20000823190906/http://soonersports.fansonly.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/okla-m-footbl-mtt.html and in a June 19, 2001 snapshot, so the same 14 names appear before, during, and after the title season with no changes. Note that soonersports.com redirected to soonersports.fansonly.com in this era; the plain soonersports.com archive URLs return only a redirect stub.

QUOTE MECHANICS - PLEASE READ. On that OU staff page the roster is a two-column HTML table: the role label sits in the left cell and the person's name is a separate link in the right cell of the same row. There is therefore NO contiguous "role + name" string anywhere in the page text, in either the raw HTML or any text/markdown conversion. Rather than fabricate a joined string that would fail a string match, I quoted the exact role-label cell text for each person and recorded the adjacent name cell in the note. The same structure ("Name:" / "Position:" label-value tables) applies to the individual OU coach bio pages under /mtt/99staff/. Where I could find prose that names a person and role in one sentence, I added it as a second source.

TIERS FULLY RECOVERED. All 10 on-field coaches (head coach + the NCAA-maximum 9 assistants): Bob Stoops, Mark Mangino, Mike Stoops, Brent Venables, Bobby Jack Wright, Jonathan Hayes, Steve Spurrier Jr., Cale Gundy, Chuck Long, Jackie Shipp. Strength and conditioning: Jerry Schmidt. Football operations/administration: Merv Johnson and Matt McMillen.

TIERS PARTIALLY RECOVERED. Graduate assistants: OU's own page lists exactly one, Brandon Blaney, and his later staff bios independently confirm 1999-2000 as an offensive GA at Oklahoma. NCAA rules of the era permitted two GAs, so a second GA very likely existed but I could not document a name; I did not guess one. Student/undergraduate assistants: only Brandon Hall is documented, via his Wikipedia biography ("Oklahoma (SA)", 1998-2000) and his inclusion in the 2000 team navbox on the Wikipedia team-season article; there were certainly other undergraduate assistants whose names are unrecoverable.

TIERS NOT RECOVERABLE FROM 2000-ERA SOURCES. Medical and equipment staff were not listed on OU's 2000 online football staff page at all. I documented Scott Anderson (head athletic trainer, at OU in that role from 1997) and Greg Tipton (equipment, promoted to Director of Athletics Equipment in 2000) from later official OU sources whose career tables span the 2000 season - but the full football sports-medicine staff (assistant trainers, team physicians, physical therapists) and the assistant equipment managers are undocumented. Also undocumented for 2000: the football video staff, any recruiting/personnel staffers below Bobby Jack Wright (who held the recruiting coordinator title concurrently with coaching defensive ends), academic support staff, and football secretarial staff. The 2007 OU spring guide notes that McMillen's job was to work "directly with OU's strength, sports medicine, football video, equipment, field maintenance and secretarial staffs," which confirms those units existed in the program but names none of their members for 2000.

ANALYSTS AND QUALITY CONTROL. No analyst or quality-control staff existed as a documented tier at Oklahoma in 2000; those categories are a later-2000s development. Zero rows in those categories is a real finding, not a gap.

SOURCES THAT DID NOT PAN OUT. The 2000 and 2001 OU football media guides are not online: soonersports.com's own media-guide archive begins with 2004 (issuu), and archive.org holds only three cover scans of the 2001 guide (item 2001-Oklahoma-Sooners-Football-Media-Guide-CS-7-bubs1085), no interior pages. No athletics-wide OU staff directory from 2000-2001 is in the Wayback Machine - the only /genrel/staff.html capture is the athletic development office, not sports medicine or equipment. The National Football Foundation's 2000 Oklahoma page names only Bob Stoops. Wayback coverage of the 2000-era OU football site is thin generally; several archived press-release URLs from fall 2000 return empty bodies.

NO MID-SEASON CHANGES. I found no evidence of anyone arriving or departing during the 2000 season, so no midseason_note is set on any row. Chuck Long and Mark Mangino's OC promotion both date to the 1999-2000 offseason (Mike Leach left for Texas Tech after 1999 and is NOT on the 2000 staff, despite his bio page persisting in the site's /99staff/ directory - a trap worth flagging for anyone re-running this).
